newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION - Gregan looks to turn table on Tonu'u.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION - Gregan looks to turn table on Tonu'u.

text.p: AUCKLAND, May 30 - Wallabies and ACT halfback George Gregan, one of the star performers in this year's Super 12 rugby competition, hopes to turn the tables on Auckland Blues opposite Ofisa Tonu'u in Saturday's final.
Tonu'u had probably his finest game of this year's Super 12 when the Blues beat the ACT Brumbies 41-29 in the round-robin match at Pukekohe.
Gregan remembers the encounter well and said he had nothing but respect for the Auckland halfback.
"He's a very good player, he has been playing consistently well as have the rest of the Auckland side," Gregan said.
"He's just one of the many good players in the Auckland team that we have to keep our eye on."
However, he hopes he won't be the spur to put Tonu'u, who has been below his best in the last two games, back on track.
"Well that is not such a good thing if I've brought the best out of him the last time," he said.
"It would be nice if I could do it the other way and bring the worst out of him in the final game of the season.
"But when you're playing good opposition it brings the best out of players and it would be the same.
"Us playing Auckland will bring the best out of the Brumbies because they (Auckland) are a class side."
Gregan warned ACT had not come to Auckland just to assist in a Blues celebration tomorrow afternoon.
"It has been a really good rise for us over the last two years," he said.
"We set our goals of making the semifinals this year and then reassessing it from there. But we never thought at the start of the year that we'd make the final.
"It is a pleasant surprise (to make the final), but once you get to the final you just can't sit back and say great, we've made the final'.
"You've got to try and win the thing and that is what we've come over here to do."
He said the Brumbies scrum, which was under immense pressure the last time the two sides met, had improved markedly and that would be seen tomorrow.
"I think it is improving. We've improved in a lot of areas since then and we've needed to if we were to progress, and we have progressed to the final," Gregan said.
"It shows we've learned a lot from that game. Before that game we hadn't played a team that put on that amount of pressure on us at the breakdown and through the game.
"They seemed to be in our face on attack and defence, we hadn't experienced that to date in the Super 12 so it was a bit of a culture shock to the guys."
However, he believed that experience and the last two weekends, when ACT beat the Wellington Hurricanes in back-to-back matches, were also invaluable.

"When we played Wellington away, if anyone was going to get intimidated and get stage fright it would have happened then, but we rose to the occasion there and repeated it in Canberra in last weekend's semifinal," Gregan said.
"So the last two weeks have been good for us in that regard."
